fields.sample_size: 174 municipalities of the Sao Paulo Macrometropolis (SPMM) from the municipal basic information survey (MUNIC) plus documents on the Corrego Limpo Program and the 2017 renewal of the Cantareira System water grant; documentary and institutional analysis
fields.effect_estimate: Of 174 municipalities, 107 declared a municipal sanitation policy, only 37 a sanitation council (27 exclusive committees, 10 shared with other councils), and only 19 a dedicated municipal sanitation fund; 128 had an approved sanitation plan, 27 were drafting one and 19 had none, and 18 of the 128 plans were prepared without other bodies' participation. The authors analyse horizontal and vertical integration, citizen participation and territory in the Corrego Limpo and Cantareira cases and argue that the division of competences among federative entities and weak participation hinder multilevel sanitation governance. Descriptive; no effect estimates.
fields.study_design: documentary and institutional case analysis of a metropolitan region with descriptive municipal survey data
fields.section: Full text: Theoretical and methodological approach; analysis of competences, municipal instruments (policy, council, fund, plan counts); Corrego Limpo and Cantareira cases
fields.exact_location: Theoretical and methodological approach; analysis of competences, municipal instruments (policy, council, fund, plan counts); Corrego Limpo and Cantareira cases

evidence_level: Single-study evidence: an institutional analysis of sanitation governance in the Sao Paulo Macrometropolis (174 municipalities), read in full text 2026-10-04. 107 have a sanitation policy, 128 a plan, but only 37 a council and 19 a fund; participation in plan making was limited. Descriptive.
pdf_note: Brazilian journal article (2020), about 66,000 characters read
notes: Abstract-level extraction accurate; adds the municipal instrument counts, which are direct descriptive evidence on planning and participation instruments under Law 11,445/2007.
